selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main question starts the imaginary discussion?
questions.answer: It asks why so much more effort is still being made for faith and tawhid when even a small part of the work is already very powerful.

questions.question: What challenge is raised about that purpose?
questions.answer: The challenge asks why more preparation is needed when the work already seems highly effective.

questions.question: What does the passage say the fortress contains?
questions.answer: It contains Islam.

questions.question: What picture is used to represent Islam in danger?
questions.answer: Islam is pictured as a giant fortress under damage.

questions.question: What has caused these deep problems in society, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Corrupting forces built up over a very long time have damaged them in a serious way.

questions.question: What social areas are mentioned after that?
questions.answer: The common heart, accepted ideas, and public conscience.

questions.question: What kind of proofs are needed for such huge spiritual damage?
questions.answer: Proofs that are extremely certain and very strong are needed.

questions.question: What kind of certainty must the needed proofs have?
questions.answer: They must have the highest level of certainty.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is one more role of the Risale-i Nur besides repairing damage?
questions.answer: It also helps people move forward through endless levels of faith.

questions.question: Why might someone be surprised by the intense effort being put into the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Because even a very small amount of it already seems enough to answer strong unbelief.

questions.question: What has been increasing, according to that questioner?
questions.answer: The large-scale preparation and readiness of the Risale-i Nur have been increasing.

questions.question: What does this image help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that the crisis is widespread and serious.

questions.question: What is one image in the passage that shows the mission is communal?
questions.answer: The image of rebuilding a huge fortress shows that the work concerns the whole community.

questions.question: What does the long time period mentioned in the passage suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the harm is deep-rooted and did not appear all at once.

questions.question: What had been prepared over many years to harm people?
questions.answer: Methods and tools of corruption had been prepared over a long period.

questions.question: How does the passage emphasize the strength needed in those proofs?
questions.answer: It compares their strength to mountains.

questions.question: What does the phrase about endless levels of faith teach us?
questions.answer: It teaches that faith can keep growing stronger and deeper.

questions.question: What two big jobs of the Risale-i Nur are mentioned?
questions.answer: It repairs major spiritual damage and helps believers rise in faith.

questions.question: In the opening of the passage, what kind of conversation is being described?
questions.answer: An imagined question-and-answer discussion.

questions.question: What two subjects is the Risale-i Nur said to be especially prepared to serve?
questions.answer: Belief and the proof of Allah’s unity.

questions.question: How does the response show that the mission is much bigger than it may first seem?
questions.answer: It says the work is dealing with massive destruction affecting Islam as a whole.

questions.question: What does the image of a citadel teach about Islam in this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches that Islam is something strong and precious that protects people, yet it has been heavily attacked.

questions.question: What do the breaches in common thought and conscience show about the problem?
questions.answer: They show that the problem has spread beyond individuals into the wider community.

questions.question: Why is this especially dangerous for the masses of believers?
questions.answer: Because many believers depend on those supports as a refuge and guide.
